notes: The both … and pair is split between מִן and עַד because no waw stands in the phrase; rule 14 assigns the closing connective to the waw only where one is written, and rule 26's reading of a בֵּין … לְ member supports giving it to the morpheme that does stand where the connective stands. The competing reading (עַד unrepresented, and added) is named in the unit's note.
אֲשֶׁר and the resumptive suffix share whereof under rule 22's fusion clause, while בְּ and תָּוֶךְ keep their own English.
